topic_summary: Analysis of the second law of thermodynamics as a fundamental physical constraint on heat engine efficiency. The second law establishes that no heat engine operating between two thermal reservoirs can be more efficient than a reversible Carnot engine, and that all real engines must be less efficient due to irreversibilities. This constraint is independent of engineering design, materials, or technological advancement.

key_entities: Second Law of Thermodynamics (fundamental physical principle governing entropy and energy conversion)
Carnot Cycle (idealized reversible heat engine establishing maximum theoretical efficiency)
Real Heat Engines (actual implementations: steam turbines, internal combustion, etc.)
Thermal Reservoirs (hot and cold temperature boundaries)
Entropy (state function measuring energy dispersal and irreversibility)
key_tensions: Theoretical maximum (Carnot efficiency) vs practical achievable efficiency (real engines)
Reversible idealization (zero entropy generation) vs irreversible reality (friction, heat loss, finite-time operation)

axes.structural_delta: Maximum theoretical efficiency determined solely by temperature ratio (1 - T_cold/T_hot), independent of working substance or mechanism
axes.primary_observable: Efficiency = (T_hot - T_cold) / T_hot for any reversible engine; measured via temperature differential
axes.selection_reason: Pure physical constraint; upstream to all engineering considerations; different observable (temperature ratio) from irreversibility measures

axes.structural_delta: Efficiency loss from irreversible processes (friction, turbulence, heat conduction across finite temperature differences) that generate entropy
axes.primary_observable: Entropy generation rate; exergy destruction; measured via (Carnot efficiency - actual efficiency)
axes.selection_reason: Different observable (entropy generation) from temperature ratio; structurally distinct physical mechanism; passes independence test

axes.structural_delta: Operating at maximum theoretical efficiency requires infinite time (zero power output); finite power requires operating below Carnot efficiency
axes.primary_observable: Power output vs efficiency curve; Curzon-Ahlborn efficiency for maximum power; measured via time-per-cycle and work output
axes.selection_reason: Different observable (time/power) from both temperature ratio and entropy generation; structurally independent constraint; passes pairwise test

axes.human_readable: Engineering Optimization Space (Design Choice Within Physical Bounds)
axes.structural_delta: Engineering decisions (materials, geometry, operating conditions) determine position within the space bounded by Carnot ceiling, irreversibility losses, and finite-time constraints
axes.primary_observable: Actual engine efficiency metrics; design parameter choices; cost-benefit analysis of efficiency improvements
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis node; different observable (design choices) from physical constraints; coordination problem distinct from physical limits

omegas.description: Do quantum heat engines operating on quantum coherence or entanglement violate or circumvent classical second law constraints? Current research suggests they remain bounded by generalized second law formulations, but this is an active research frontier.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - quantum regime not addressed in classical thermodynamics framing

omegas.description: Can information-theoretic engines (Maxwell's demon with feedback control, Szilard engine) extract work beyond classical limits? Landauer's principle suggests information erasure costs restore second law, but boundary cases remain contested.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - information as thermodynamic resource not cataloged

omegas.description: Does the second law's status as 'mountain' depend on cosmological boundary conditions (low-entropy Big Bang)? If universe had different initial conditions, would heat engine constraints differ? This probes whether the constraint is truly fundamental or contingent on our universe's history.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) - analysis assumes standard cosmological context without examination

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. All four axes represent distinct physical constraints with different observables: temperature ratio (carnot_efficiency_ceiling), entropy generation (irreversibility_gap), time/power tradeoff (finite_time_tradeoff), and design choice space (engineering_optimization_space). Each passes pairwise independence testing. Three omegas document frontier physics questions beyond classical thermodynamics scope.
